references.text: Evil among people was great on the earth, and God saw that human thoughts and intentions were evil all the time - this shows the pattern of corruption that Moses warns about.
Israel's worship of the golden calf demonstrates the corruption and turning away from God's way that Moses predicts will happen after his death.
Moses warns that the people will do what is evil in the Lord's sight and provoke him to anger with the work of their hands, which leads to disaster.
Moses reminds the people that they have been rebellious against the Lord from the day he knew them - this confirms his knowledge of their tendency to stray.
Moses' song describes how the people will become corrupt and act foolishly toward the Lord.
Joshua warns the people that they will abandon the Lord and serve foreign gods, and then disaster will strike them.
After the judge's death, the people turned away and acted worse than their fathers - this fulfills Moses' prophecy of corruption after his death.
Solomon did what was evil in the Lord's sight and provoked him to anger - fulfilling the warning about doing evil in the Lord's sight.
Isaiah describes a sinful people who have abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.
Hosea describes Israel's apostasy in the last days and their return to the Lord in the end times.

Paul warns the elders at Ephesus that after his departure, savage wolves will come among them and men will arise with false teaching - a similar pattern of corruption following the leader's departure.
Paul describes the corruption in the last days, when people will be self-centered and ungodly - this corresponds to 'in the last days' in Deuteronomy.
Peter warns about false teachers who will bring corruption among the people, reflecting Moses' warning of corruption.
